_rule: Round 5 of the filing readings (decision rules of 23 October 2026, a decision of the Claude analysis session, results/extraction_error_rate/mature-cohort/round5/rules.md). 'excluded' (rule 1 or rule 4b; each entry names its rule). Rule 1: a record leaves the PRIMARY sample (outcome 'mature_cohort') when its year t development table's history (an underwriting year u <= t-2, or the table as a whole) differs from the year t-1 report beyond the exchange rate with no explanation in either filing; AND the year t table fails the year's accounts (implied gross incurred off by more than 10% beyond what its basis explains; the paid test decides only where the table gives no implied incurred) while the year t-1 control ties (within 5%; or within 10% when the same basis gap explains both years, an '& prior' column outside the cells or an ultimate basis against earned accounts, and the year t miss is at least three times the control's); AND the year t-1 report's printed base does not give a figure that reconciles either. Rule 4b (a table its own cells prove inconsistent, added 24 October 2026 after the round-8 readings): where rule 1's control does not tie, a record still leaves the PRIMARY sample when (i) both readings report that the year t table prints, for an underwriting year u <= t-2, cumulative paid lower than the year t-1 report printed for the same year, by more than the exchange rate explains and with no explanation in either filing (a reading reports the fall when it quotes both cells for the same underwriting year, whether or not it names it); (ii) the year t table fails the year's accounts by more than 10% (rule 1's test); and (iii) no base gives a figure that reconciles (rule 3 fails). Incurred first (added 24 October 2026 after the review of the fixes): rule 1's accounts test and rule 4b's (ii) use the implied gross incurred test wherever the table gives one; the paid test decides only where the table gives no implied incurred, because M is an incurred movement and a paid cell M does not use cannot make M unmeasured. Rules 1 to 7 were written before the adjudication; rule 5b, rule 6's take-on clause (take_on_table_unreconciled), rule 1's exact control clause and rule 4b were added after particular readings or review 8 (rules.md names them). The exact control clause, made exact on 23 October 2026 after review 8 and re-applied to every record: on 23 October it moved no record (4242/2022 moved from rule 1 to rule 3 on review 8's decision to set aside the merged '2016 & Prior' column; its control, -1.1%, ties under either reading); applied to the round-8 readings Z7 and Z8 it takes 780/2016 and 4747/2024 out of rule 1. Rule 4b, applied to the readings of every record of rounds 5 to 8 (round8/rule_4b_scan.json), decides two records: 4747/2024 and 2232/2017. The loader (run_analysis.py) removes an 'excluded' entry's record at the unusable-severity step with the tag RESTATED_BASE_TABLE and counts it (restated_base_excluded); under outcome 'precedence_672' the register is not read and nothing changes. 'history_restated' (rule 6): the table ties to the year's accounts (or its basis explains the gap), but an underwriting year u <= t-2 moved beyond the exchange rate without explanation by more than 1% of R (unexplained_history_move), or the two readings disagree on the validity label (valid, screen_misread, units_slip against restated_base, undeterminable) but not on the facts (label_disagreement), or (rule 5b) the filing prints no transferred gross amount for a take-on in year t but bounds it at or below 10% of R (take_on_base_bounded), or an explained take-on already in R has a table that does not reconcile with the filing's own roll-forward (take_on_table_unreconciled), or the record's corrected figure is the session's derivation from cells both readers quote, a figure neither reader gives (derived_correction); the record stays in the primary and src/check_low_confidence_sensitivity.py leaves it out of its least-certain refit. 'takeon_unmeasurable' (rule 5b, decision of the Claude analysis session, 23 October 2026): a record leaves the PRIMARY sample when an RITC, LPT or merger effective in year t, whose acquired history the table shows as if always, is not in the opening gross claims outstanding R, the filing does not print the transferred gross reserves, and the readings show the acquired share of the base could exceed 10% of R (an unmeasurable take-on, as 1861/2020 and 1084/2022 are); the loader removes the entry's record at the unusable-severity step with the tag TAKEON_BASE_UNMEASURABLE and counts it (takeon_base_unmeasurable_excluded); under outcome 'precedence_672' nothing changes. A take-on the filing bounds at or below 10% of R stays and is listed under history_restated. 'source_history_set_aside' (rule 8, the source-history rule of 26 October 2026, the recommendation of the Codex analysis adopted on Colin's instruction and applied by the Claude analysis session; found during Codex's tail investigation of 6131/2021, post hoc, and applied to the census population chosen by source features): a record leaves the PRIMARY sample when specific source evidence raises a material unresolved concern about overlapping claims history, gross/net mixing or cohort reassignment through closure and the declared gross original-cohort outcome cannot be defensibly reconstructed or validated, whatever its size or sign; the loader gives it no figure and the tag SOURCE_HISTORY_SET_ASIDE and counts it (source_history_set_aside), under outcome 'precedence_672' nothing changes. Every entry rests on two independent readings of the filing (and the tie-break readings where the first two disagreed on the facts), with the pages and quotes. Built by src/build_restated_base_excluded.py from the archived readings.

readings.note: Both tables carry the same heading and basis wording, both reconcile to their balance-sheet gross claims outstanding, and no restatement note or 2023 transaction exists, so presentation alone is not explained; yet the 2023 table's historical incurred and paid cells for UYs 2020-21 are higher than the 2022 print by amounts that net to zero in outstanding (end-2022 incurred 253,729 vs 192,060; paid implied 144,792 vs 83,123), and the 2023 table's year-on-year movement exceeds the 2023 income statement's total gross incurred by 35.7m. M = +42.378m therefore rests on a rebased history (largely the 2021 column, +39.5m) that is not 2023 development, and using the 2022 diagonal (104m) is worse. Not an RITC/transfer (none in 2023). Possible 'development' reading is not supported by the income statement tie-out. The paid history is also unexplained: the 2023 table's cumulative paid rose 133,076 across 2020-2023 rows vs gross claims paid of 36,123 in 2023, on the 2022 base; so the filings contain an unexplained inconsistency in the earlier years of the table. Recommend excluding or treating as undeterminable-for-M-size if a conservative rule is preferred; my reading is restated_base.

In the 2022 report the diagonal at end-2022 is on the booked basis (it ties to 55,574) while the earlier cells are Syndicate 2689's: the 2022 table implies a 2022 incurred of -28.2m (57,689-71,562, 78,715-89,084, 60,403-64,390) against accounts 22,748 paid - 27,481 provision = -4.7m, because the take-on premium (£75.2m) was below 2689's own estimate.

The year t table's own two diagonals reproduce the year's gross incurred (2.3%) and the gross claims outstanding at both dates reconcile by a roll-forward (55,574 + 56,161 - 225 = 111,510; RITC line nil in 2023). The booked development of the taken-on years in 2023 is +8.7m, adverse (the report states 'Net prior year reserves on US casualty business were strengthened during 2023'), against M of +10.5m. readings.reason: The concern is the earlier inward RITC of Syndicate 2689's 2017-2019 years (effective 1 January 2022) and a restated end-2022 diagonal in the 2023 table against the 2022 report (about 23m above on a like-for-like rate, with cumulative payments also restated). It is resolved at the level of M because the 2023 table's incurred ties to the accounts (2.3%), its closing provision ties exactly, and an independent bridge from the opening provision, 2023 payments and closing provision gives +8.7m for these cohorts against the table's +10.5m. wording.represented: p14, 'Representation of notes to the Accounts': "The notes to the accounts have been represented to align to the Corporation of Lloyds mandated disclosure. Unless otherwise stated there is no restatement of any figures." This is a statement of a change of presentation with no restatement. A literal reading would restate UW2021 end-2023 by +49% and UW2023 first-year by -34% against the 2023 report with no explanation, which the sentence rules out. A layout change in which the triangle was turned on its side (rows = UW years) while the headings kept the old axes is what the sentence and the overlay jointly imply.
wording.pure_underwriting_year: p51 'Pure underwriting year' is the label of the left column of the table (the Lloyd's mandated heading for an underwriting-year basis table); it says the estimates are on a UW-year (ultimate, unearned included) basis, not which axis holds the years. It does not describe a reallocation between years; no wording of a reallocation between underwriting years appears in either filing (2024 text searched for 'restat', 'reallocat', 're-present', 'represented', 'pure underwriting year').
wording.paid_row_caveat: The printed 'Less gross claims paid' line has one value per printed column (11,286 | 48,102 | 3,698 | 3,931). Read by column heads these are UW 2021-2024 paid; if the body is transposed the paid line may be mis-bound too. It does not enter M and its total (67,017) is axis-independent, so the caveat does not change M or the reconciliation.

readings.what_translation_can_explain: Nothing in the observed direction. The table says paid is at historical rates and reserves are restated at the latest (end-2017) rate, so the end-2016 cell should equal cum paid + opening reserve at end-2017 rates. The accounts' own exchange line moves the gross provision DOWN by 647 in 2017 (p29: 14,059, (1,711), (647), 11,701; 7,861 of the opening 14,059 is US dollar, p24). So the end-2016 cells should be about 53,853 + 13,412 = 67,265, not 68,814: the printed cells are 1,549 (2.3% of cells, 11.0% of R) higher, and FX works the wrong way to explain it. Even with no retranslation at all the expected cells are 53,853 + 14,059 = 67,912 (still 902 short of the printed 68,814). A whole-cell retranslation at the year's FX would lower, not raise, the end-2016 cells (-647/14,059 = -4.6%).

roll_forward_reconstruction.method: Opening gross provision 14,059 + 2017 gross incurred 559 - gross paid 2,270 + exchange (647) = 11,701 (ties to the pound). All of the 2017 gross incurred belongs to the 2011/2012 rows plus at most the 2017 year's own new business (GWP 104, earned 104), so M(u<=2015, FX-neutral) = +559 (an upper bound; at most about 0.1m of it is the 2017 year's own claims). Equivalent by cells: end-2017 cells 67,824 = (cum paid end-2016 53,853 + opening 14,059 - 647) + 559 exactly.
roll_forward_reconstruction.base: gross claims incurred in the 2017 technical account less nothing (FX is carried on the separate exchange line, so 559 is FX-neutral); R = 14,059

readings.verdict_figure: M = +0.56m (+4.0% of R=14,059). The printed -0.99m is NOT validated: its end-2016 diagonal overstates the opening gross reserves by 0.9m (no FX) to 1.5m (with FX), FX cannot explain the direction, and its implied 2017 incurred (-990) has the opposite sign to the accounts' 559 and to the report's own 'strengthening' narrative. If the rule can only accept the printed figure, set the printed -0.99m aside and use the accounts roll-forward +0.56m.
readings.reason: The concern is the internal closing (2014 year into 2017) and an end-2016 diagonal that does not tie to the opening balance sheet. The outcome is reconstructed from the technical account and the provision reconciliation, which tie exactly to the closing provision, giving +0.56m. The sign of the printed figure is wrong on this evidence. Residual weakness: the 2016 report is absent, so the cause of the overstated end-2016 cells (and the cohort split of 559) cannot be read.
readings.conflict_with_other_readings: Reading A (end-2016 cells overstated by about 1.5m, M = +0.56m) is confirmed. Reading B (difference within sterling retranslation) is refuted: the exchange line is negative (-647) and would lower the end-2016 cells.

explanation.syndicate_958: 2017 p5: 'With effect from the 2016 year of account, CMA merged Syndicate 958's capacity into Syndicate 4444. explanation.fx: No exchange rate is printed. Direction from the filing: 2017 p5 lists 'the partial recovery of the value of Sterling against the US Dollar' (Sterling stronger: US dollar amounts become fewer pounds); US dollar technical provisions are 1,227,673 of 2,003,465 = 61% (2017 p31). The accounts' own translation effect on gross claims outstanding in 2017 is a reduction of 33,144 (balance sheet movement 346,658 less change in provision 379,802, p13/p16), 2.8% of the opening 1,200,561. So a stronger Sterling should lower the end-2016 cells in the 2017 table; they are 4.7% (2011, 2012) and 3.9% (2013) HIGHER and only 2014-2016 are within a few percent. In the control year the cells moved with the currency: the 2016 table's end-2015 cells are 2.3% to 10.7% higher than the 2015 print (2011 351,980 vs 344,242 = 1.0225; 2012 363,811 vs 351,920 = 1.0338; 2013 372,441 vs 356,540 = 1.0446; 2014 385,327 vs 360,033 = 1.0703; 2015 240,706 vs 217,535 = 1.1065), in a year the 2016 report describes as 'a fall in the value of Sterling against the US Dollar following the UK's decision to leave the European Union' (2016 p5). That is the direction an FX rise would give, and the size is plausible for the share of US dollar business. 2017 moves the other way in the old years, so currency does not explain it.

readings.reconciliation_of_2016_base_to_2017_acco: No. Latest 2017 cells less the 2016 printed base give 1,112.6m (+10.3%) or 1,169.3m (+15.9% with 2010&prior) against gross incurred of 1,008.5m, and the gap widens once the base is retranslated to end-2017 rates. readings.verdict_detail: The 2017 table's end-2016 history is not the 2016 report's history and the change is not explained. Individual cells move by up to +4.7% (older years) and -22.5% (2015 at age 0), outside the range sterling retranslation can produce (+3.5% to -8.1% per the p36 rates) and opposite in sign to the dominant US-dollar effect, and the ratio rises smoothly with age rather than being constant per currency mix. The filing states no restatement, correction or change of basis. The incurred test misses 5% (+6.3% against a -1.1% control), the paid proxy is +30.8% (control -6.2%; mixed-base because the 2017 table prints no end-2016 payments), and the claims reconciliation carries an unexplained 'Other 37,196'. The Syndicate 958 RITC is effective 1 Jan 2018 (p5), so it is unlikely to be in the end-2016 cells, but acceptance on 31 Dec 2017 (p7) and the unexplained 'Other' leave a small unresolved doubt. The movement is not measurable from the table with confidence: M is +118.2m on the 2017 table's own cells and +167.7m on the 2016 printed base (u 2011-2015), a 29% spread, and the filing prints no gross mature-cohort movement. 'Valid' (stated adverse development) is right about the sign (p25: 'in 2017 gross and net deteriorations occurred') but not about the base.
readings.note: Why not valid: criteria need the table to tie to the accounts (incurred within 5%) and any history change explained or immaterial; neither holds. Why not stronger than moderate: the history change is small (1.8% of the diagonal, 3.4% of opening reserves), the table's balance to pay ties exactly to the balance sheet, the own-cell incurred miss is only 6.3%, and the incurred test is blunt here (basis-adjusted control -8.1%). If the analysis keeps the record it should use the table's own two diagonals (+118.2m) and flag the sensitivity to the 2016 base (+167.7m); the author should decide. Same age-dependent drift appears (smaller) from the 2015 report to the 2016 table (end-2015 cells 1.023, 1.034, 1.045, 1.070, 1.107 times the 2015 latest), where the US dollar rose against sterling (FX ceiling far larger), so that year is consistent with FX.

(2) The history in the 2022 table is a real, stated structural rebase: the 2022 RITC of Syndicate 5678's years and the Hiscox ADC bring about 270m of gross liabilities (closing claims outstanding 489.6m against 221.9m a year earlier) into columns for earlier underwriting years, and the table is a pro-forma combined book (cumulative paid history of the acquired books included). The year's accounts show the RITC/ADC through claims (353.8m gross incurred), which the table cannot reproduce (141.0m implied from its own diagonals), so the table is not tied to the year's accounts and the filing prints no stand-alone movement on the opening book. M = 9.1m therefore measures the 2022 development of the combined (opening plus acquired) book against a denominator R = 221.9m that covers only the opening book (the acquired liabilities are not in R); the same scale problem as 3500_2023. The explanation exists, so it is not a silent restatement; the figure is not a like-for-like prior-year movement on the opening reserves.

readings.selection_event: Outward split RITC: 'On 7 February 2018 Lloyd's issued a direction ... to allow a Split RITC of Syndicate 1084's 2015 Year of Account. Syndicate 1084 entered into an RITC of the part of the 2015 Year of Account which comprised the UK Division book of business with Antares Syndicate 1274 ... the UK Division closing reserves at 31 December 2017 were net nil (gross GBP 199.7m) and therefore the RITC was for a nominal consideration of GBP 1' (p6). Technical reserves note p28: 'RITC of the UK Division - (199.7)' in gross claims outstanding and '(199.7)' in reinsurers' share. The reserves are those at 31 Dec 2017, so the transfer is at the opening of 2018: between the end-2017 and end-2018 diagonals (inside the movement M measures). It covers UK Division liabilities of the 2015 YoA, which include all earlier pure years (2010 & prior to 2015).
readings.overlapping_history: Yes, a transfer sits inside the two diagonals. The end-2017 cells in the 2018 table are the 2017 report's cells retranslated only (2011: 588.9 vs 586.6 printed in 2017; 2012 457.9 vs 455.9; 2013 543.1 vs 538.9; 2014 722.9 vs 714.6; 2015 570.4 vs 558.6; 2016 503.3 vs 488.3; factors x1.004-x1.031, rising with recency = FX), so they are PRE-RITC, whereas the end-2018 cells are post-RITC (table reserves 1,965.4 tie to the post-RITC balance sheet). The prior-year movement is therefore reduced by the transferred gross reserves, which the table does not allocate by pure year. Gross-minus-net movement for 2011-2016: gross -134.0 vs net (end-2017 -> end-2018: 2011 423.9->418.3; 2012 326.8->325.8; 2013 390.7->382.6; 2014 468.6->473.0; 2015 378.5->387.5; 2016 374.3->412.3 = +36.7), difference -170.7, i.e. about 85% of the 199.7 sits in these six cohorts and the remainder in '2010 and prior'.
readings.gross_net: RITC was gross 199.7 and net nil: the gross table falls by the transferred reserves while the net table (which the outward reinsurance mirrors) does not (net prior-year movements 2011-2015 -10.2 in total vs gross -185.1). So the gross cells carry an item that the net cells do not: a gross/net asymmetry created by the transfer, not a net figure in a gross row.

Total u<=2016 movement ex-transfer = accounts incurred 698.2 less the 2017 cohort 267.9 less the 2018 cohort 420.5 = +9.8 (GBP m, inclusive of '2010 and prior'), but this relies on the table identity at year-end rates (+/- 15) and cannot be split by cohort; the declared figure -134.0 (2011-2016) is not recoverable because the RITC's split across cohorts and the '2010 and prior' share are not printed.
readings.reason: A gross 199.7m (10% of opening reserves) outward RITC falls between the diagonals and is deducted from the gross pure-year estimates (end-2018) but not from the end-2017 cells; the 2011-2016 gross movement (-134.0m) is swamped by it, net is unaffected (net nil), and the filing prints no split by cohort. The control year ties, so the mismatch is the transfer; no defensible per-cohort reconstruction exists.

readings.reconstruction_test_from_sources: Tried and failed on levels. Sources: 3000's own 2015 table (2015 filing p.36, original rates) and 1400's 2015 table (1400 2015 filing p.32, gross, columns 2011-2013). Outstanding at end 2015 ties exactly: restated 85,693+143,688+153,716 = 383,097 against 3000's SFP provisions 53,040+87,540+92,385 = 232,965 plus 1400's 32,653+56,147+61,331 = 150,131, total 383,096. Cumulative incurred does not: end-2015 cells for 2011-2013 in the 2016 table total 584,362+445,510+343,050 = 1,372,922 against 3000 226,131+193,364+176,227 = 595,722 plus 1400 109,204+110,323+104,076 = 323,603, i.e. 919,325 (restated 453,597 or 49% higher). Cumulative paid shows the same excess: 498,669+301,822+189,334 = 989,825 against 364,131 + 176,616 = 540,747 (+449,078). By age the 2011 column's ratio to own-plus-1400 is 1.016, 1.058, 1.219, 1.407, 1.743 (ages 0-4), which a revaluation cannot produce, and the 2013 column runs 148,632 / 203,006 / 343,050 against own-plus-1400 of 146,301 / 272,944 / 280,303. So the 2016 table's older cells are not the sum of the two printed histories; the liability by cohort at end 2015 is, but cumulative incurred and paid carry an unexplained excess that varies by age. M is a difference of cumulative incurred between end 2015 and end 2016 (paid plus outstanding movement), so it is not shown to be distorted, but it cannot be shown to be clean either.

earlier_listing.facts: added after review 8 (decision of the Claude analysis session, 23 October 2026), on the same all-prior-years scope as 3500/2023. RITCs of Syndicates 1897, 2468 and 1980/2014/2001 effective 1 January 2022 and loss portfolio transfers (p4; note 7 p30 'Reinsurance of new liabilities 1,728,476'), the history carried as if always (the 2018 column about double the 2021 report's, Q7). But the table does not reconcile with note 7's change in estimates including foreign exchange of -293.1m (-293,072, p30) on that scope: the movement on every column that existed at end-2021 (2013-2019 and 2021) is -291.756m - 98.057m = -389.8m (review 8; P6's workings), and the whole table (those columns plus the new 2022 column, +363.424m) is -26.4m, a gap of 266.7m (P6; Q7 -26.389m); only the 2013-2019 columns alone (-291.8m, the adopted figure) are within 0.4% of it. LPT placement conflict: P6 reads the mid-2022 loss portfolio transfers of Syndicates 1200 (293.8m) and 1686 (67.1m) as entering the history as if always, while the ninth census (data/opening_reserves_takeon_base.json) places all four LPTs (also 2468's 22.6m and 2001's 5.2m: 388.7m) in the 2022 column, outside M and outside R. Either way the acquired share outside R is at most 9.1% of R for the two mid-2022 LPTs (360.9m of 3,955.045m) and 9.8% with all four (388.7m), at or below rule 5b's 10%, so rule 5b would list the record too. readings.control_prior_year: 2017 control: table-implied incurred 93,230 v accounts 81,429 (+14.5%, residual about +20% after FX): also not tied; 2016 control tied within FX (see 6111_2016).
readings.reconstruction: Not validated. Closing table reserves 159,344 equal gross claims outstanding 159,344 (p34) and the opening diagonal matches the 2017 report up to FX, but the year's table increments (incurred 45.1m, paid about 92.5m) do not agree with the accounts' incurred 32.1m and paid 47.2m and the roll-forward's FX line is distorted by the settlement; no cohort paid at the opening is printed to rebuild M.
readings.stated_prior_year_line: Note 5 (p34): 'An unfavorable run-off deviation (prior accident years' increase) of GBP 6.0m (2017: unfavorable of 4.7m) ... wholly in respect of reserve movements on the 2016 year of account and prior'. Table gross M 21.1m, net M 26.6m for the same cohorts: the stated line is about a quarter of the table's mature movement.
readings.reason: A closure settlement of the 2015 cohort (paid set equal to the end-2017 estimate, then a negative reserve) falls between the diagonals, and the table's year-t movements do not tie to the accounts (implied incurred 45.1m v 32.1m, paid about 92.5m v 47.2m, FX line distorted) while the stated net run-off (6.0m) is a quarter of the table's net mature movement (26.6m). M (10.6% of R) cannot be validated or rebuilt. Moderate confidence: the evidence is numerical, not an explicit statement of overlap; 2017 shows the same pattern.

readings.item2_selection_event: Two annual venture closures at the two diagonal dates. 2020 report p35: 'The SPA will RITC into the 2019 YOA. The host will collect £2,130,741 from the member in 2021, in relation to the 2018 year of account losses'; 2021 report p37 note 16: 'The SPA will RITC into the 2020 YOA. The host will collect £3,132,803 from the member in 2022, in relation to the 2019 year of account losses in US Dollars. The RITC value will be passed through to the SPA 2020 experience account.' The 2021 report p6 return-on-capacity table shows 2019 YOA 'Closed', result (3,133), capacity 12,000. So the 2018 venture closed at 31 Dec 2020 (opening diagonal) and the 2019 venture at 31 Dec 2021 (closing diagonal); selected cohorts u <= 2019 are exactly those two ventures. The closing accounts for 2018 and 2019 are not in the corpus.
readings.item3_overlap: Yes, in the 2018 and 2019 rows. (a) The 2019 row's cumulative paid rises 5,142 (2020 report p32) -> 11,984 (2021 report p32), +6,842 in one calendar year, which exceeds the whole year's gross claims paid of 6,515 (p15); the 2019 row's incurred rises +5,421 in 2021 against +6,273 in 2020 while the calendar year's total gross incurred fell from 11,133 to 6,882. (b) The 2018 row's net paid, 2,028 at end-2020 (2020 report p32; gross paid 3,577), becomes 4,114 at end-2021, equal to gross paid 4,114 (p32-33); the net 2018 row jumps 2,400 -> 4,164 (+1,764) while the gross row moves +196. Reinsurance recoveries on the closed 2018 venture are thus eliminated in 2021 on the net side and the 2019 row is loaded with the closing items of the 2019 venture, consistent with the batch's bridge-bundle reading that the 2019 cumulative paid reproduces the old closed-venture gross paid plus the outgoing RITC premium (the bridge bundle itself was not opened).
readings.item4_gross_net: 2018 row: gross paid = net paid = 4,114 at end-2021 (they differed at 3,577 vs 2,028 at end-2020). Net M +7.6m against gross +5.6m; net reinsurers' share of cumulative incurred on 2018 falls from 2,100 (4,500-2,400) to 532 (4,696-4,164) in a year. Gross and net are not on a consistent basis between the two diagonals.

item5_accounts_test.control_t_minus_1_2020: 2020: incurred -3.6 per cent, paid -3.4 per cent (see 6131_2020); 2019: -2.2 and -1.7 per cent. 2021 is the first year the table fails.
item5_accounts_test.accounts_implied_M: If the 2020 and 2021 cells (878 and 4,569) are right, the accounts leave 6,882 - 878 - 4,569 = 1,435 for the 2018 and 2019 rows, against M = 5,617; the excess (about 4.2m) is of the size of the 2019 venture's RITC (£3.13m) plus the 2018 venture's net/gross paid adjustment (£2.1m).

readings.item6_reconstruction: No. Closing outstanding by cohort ties to note 4 (7,049), but the cumulative cells do not reproduce the year's claims paid or incurred: the 2019 row alone adds more paid than the whole calendar year, and the 2018 net row converts at closure. An accounts-based M (about 1.4m) depends on the other two cohorts' cells being right and is not independent. No closing account is in the corpus to bridge the 2018 and 2019 rows.
readings.reason: Specific source evidence (not the SPA status): the 2021 table's implied gross paid and incurred overshoot the accounts by about 61 per cent when the 2019 venture closes (31 Dec 2021, RITC into 2020 YOA) and the 2018 net row converts to gross after its closure, while 2018-2020 tests all pass; the 2019 row's +5.4m inflates M (5.6m, against opening gross outstanding 6.7m) and no bridge in the filings validates it.

readings.2_selection_event: SPA vehicle (S1) with serial closures. p37 note 16: 'The SPA will RITC into the 2020 YOA. The host will collect 3,132,803 from the member in 2022, in relation to the 2019 year of account losses in US Dollars. The RITC value will be passed through to the SPA 2020 experience account.' So the 2019 year closes by RITC into the 2020 YOA at 31 December 2021 (end of year t). The 2020 report (p35) had already said the 2018 YOA would RITC into 2019 with the host collecting 2,130,741 from the member in 2021 'in relation to the 2018 year of account losses', i.e. during year t (2021) the 2018 venture was closed into the 2019 venture. Both closures lie between or at the end of the diagonals.
readings.3_overlap: Yes, in the paid and incurred figures. Cumulative gross paid in the table at end 2021 is 4,114 + 11,984 + 1,568 + 1,852 = 19,518. The same cohorts at end 2020 (2020 report p32) were 3,577 + 5,142 + 278 = 8,997, so the table implies 10,521 paid in 2021, against gross claims paid of 6,515 in the 2021 accounts (p15): 61.5% too much (excess about 4.0m). Through the calendar accounts the cumulative gross paid should be 3,260 (end 2019, 2019 report p31) + 5,880 + 6,515 = 15,655 against 19,518 (+24.7%); at end 2020 the same sum ties (9,140 against 8,997, -1.6%), so the excess arises only in 2021. On the net table (p33) cumulative net paid is 4,114 + 9,367 + 285 + 1,800 = 15,566 against the accounts' 2,162 + 5,418 + 2,564 = 10,144 (excess 5,422), which is close to the sum of the two outgoing closing amounts quoted in the post balance sheet notes (2,130,741 for the 2018 YOA in 2021 and 3,132,803 for the 2019 YOA, together 5,263). The 2018 row's net paid rose from 2,028 (2020 report) to 4,114 (+2,086 against a gross rise of 537) and now equals its gross paid (4,114): the closure amount is inside the 2018 and 2019 rows' paid and so inside their cumulative incurred.
readings.4_gross_net: Yes. The 2018 row has gross paid equal to net paid (4,114 and 4,114, p32 and p33) although the 2020 report had gross 3,577 against net 2,028, and its net paid grew by 2,086 in 2021 against a gross growth of 537; the 2019 row's net paid grew from 5,142 to 9,367 (+4,225) in a year when the whole account's net claims paid were 2,564. A net closing (RITC) amount appears in the cumulative paid rows that M's cohorts use.

readings.6_reconstruction: No. The excess (about 4.0m gross paid, 4.2m incurred, 5.4m net paid) sits in the 2019 and 2018 cohort rows, and the pages give no split of the closing amounts by cohort or between gross and net; the 2019 row alone contributes 5,421 of M's 5,617. The closing accounts for the 2018 and 2019 years of account are not in the corpus (only the annual reports syndicate_6131_2018 to 2021 are). The calendar accounts give year totals only, so the cohort movement cannot be rebuilt from them.
readings.reason: Specific evidence from the filing's own figures: the table's 2021 paid and incurred movements exceed the 2021 accounts by about 4.0 to 4.2m gross (61%), the excess matches the closing (RITC) amounts the notes name, and the 2018 and 2019 rows carry net amounts (gross paid equal to net paid on the 2018 row). The mature outcome of 5.6m (84% of opening reserves) rests mainly on the 2019 row that carries the closure, and neither the closing accounts nor any roll-forward is available to rebuild it.
